question: A team lead grants "Can edit" access on a shared project to everyone who might ever open it, rather than giving most people "Can view". What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The project's chat history becomes visible to the whole organisation regardless of the access levels granted.
B) Only one editor can open the project at a time, so members are blocked whenever a colleague is in it.
C) Editors are billed separately for the project, so the department's costs rise with each person added.
D) Anyone can change the instructions and the knowledge, so the shared setup can drift without anyone noticing.
correct_answers: D) Anyone can change the instructions and the knowledge, so the shared setup can drift without anyone noticing.
explanations: Granting edit access to named people does not publish the project organisation-wide.
There is no single-editor lock on a shared project.
Access levels within a project are not billed individually.
Correct. Broad edit rights let the agreed direction and sources be altered silently by any of the members.
